snip.t: The World Health Organization’s (WHO) definitions of osteoporosis is based on BMD( bone mineral density) measurements:
Osteoporosis / fractures: Reduced bone mineral density — Calcium + vitamin D, weight‑bearing exercise, DEXA screening
Bone mineral density 6–12 months after definitive therapy for hyperparathyroidism.
Cardiovascular risk assessment (lipids, BP) — • Bone mineral density every 1–2 years if on long‑term steroids
Bone mineral density (DXA): Osteoporosis — T‑score ≤‑2.5 → high fracture risk
| Bone mineral density (if available) | Chronic vitamin D/calcium deficiency | T‑score ≤‑2.5 = osteopenia/osteoporosis |
More than 10 million adults age 50 years and older had osteoporosis and more than 43 million had low bone mineral density (BMD)
Most, but not all, studies have shown T1DM to be associated with low bone mineral density.

qs.q: A postmenopausal female undergoes evaluation for osteoporosis following a low-impact vertebral fracture. Which cellular imbalance primarily accounts for her bone mineral density loss?
o: Decreased expression of receptor activator of RANKL
Increased rate of osteoclastic bone resorption
Impaired collagen matrix production by osteoblasts
qs.e: Estrogen deficiency leads to enhanced osteoclastogenesis and accelerated bone resorption outpacing osteoblastic formation.

qs.q: A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman undergoes evaluation for decreased bone mineral density resulting from gonadal hormone deficiency. Which form of primary osteoporosis is characterized by this specific mechanism?
qs.e: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is a primary form driven specifically by estrogen deficiency leading to accelerated bone turnover. Senile osteoporosis is primarily linked to aging and impaired calcium absorption rather than estrogen withdrawal.

qs.q: An imaging modality is chosen to calculate bone mineral density (BMD) at the lumbar spine, hip, and proximal femur. Which imaging technique is standard for this purpose?
qs.e: DXA is the standard method used to calculate BMD at the lumbar spine, hip, and proximal femur. Quantitative ultrasonography has no radiation but is not as accurate as DXA.

qs.q: An imaging modality is selected to calculate bone mineral density at the lumbar spine, hip, and proximal femur. Which imaging technique is standard for this application?
qs.e: Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) is specifically used to calculate BMD at the lumbar spine, hip, and proximal femur. Quantitative ultrasonography does not measure these specific anatomical sites with the same accuracy.

qs.q: Which imaging modality is specifically used to calculate bone mineral density (BMD) at the lumbar spine, hip, and proximal femur?
qs.e: Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) is the standard method used to calculate BMD at the lumbar spine, hip, and proximal femur. While quantitative ultrasonography involves no radiation, it is not as accurate as DXA.

qs.q: A clinical team is reviewing diagnostic imaging options for a patient with suspected bone disease. Which imaging modality is specifically used to calculate bone mineral density at the lumbar spine, hip, and proximal femur?
qs.e: DXA is used to calculate BMD at the lumbar spine, hip, and proximal femur. Plain radiography and MRI do not directly calculate standardized bone mineral density values at these precise skeletal sites.
